issues.description: Delimiter table conflates literal characters and OpenAPI symbolic style names in one namespace.
issues.detail: _PARAM_VALUE_DELIMITERS mixes identity entries (',':',', '|':'|', ' ':' ') with symbolic aliases ('pipeDelimited','spaceDelimited') under one dict. A clean structure is a small allowed-char set plus a tiny alias map {'pipeDelimited':'|','spaceDelimited':' '}. This would make the precondition expressible in one line, avoid future key collisions, and let a Literal/Enum carry the type.

issues.description: ValueError raised on unsupported delimiter is undocumented and conflates developer errors with client errors.
issues.detail: The new precondition raises ValueError, but the Raises section only documents HTTPBadRequest, and the same channel reserved for malformed client input now also carries programmer mistakes. Either declare the ValueError in the Raises clause, raise TypeError, or assert at call time so the two failure modes are distinct.

issues.description: delimiter silently no-ops when the param value is already a list, weakening the postcondition.
issues.detail: When a parameter arrives multiple times, items is already a list and delimiter is silently ignored. Caller asked for splitting and got something else. The Note documents it, but the contract would be cleaner if delimiter also re-split list elements or explicitly rejected the combination.

issues.description: Stringly-typed delimiter argument should be a Literal or Enum.
issues.detail: delimiter='pipeDelimited' is a magic string validated only at runtime. A Literal union or small Enum would let the type checker enforce the precondition and document the domain at the signature, removing the need for a runtime dict lookup against a hybrid namespace.

issues.description: Tests miss boundary cases that would lock the contract.
issues.detail: Added tests cover happy paths and one rejection but do not probe: missing param with delimiter set (default path), empty-string value, single token with no delimiter, trailing delimiter, or interaction with keep_blank_qs_values. Small additions would establish the invariant rather than just demonstrate examples.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees the feature is small, well-scoped, and lands cleanly. The dominant concern is the shape of _PARAM_VALUE_DELIMITERS: it mixes literal delimiter characters with OpenAPI symbolic style names in a single dict, which all three reviewers flag as a leaky abstraction better expressed as an allowed-char set plus a tiny alias map (or a Literal/Enum). Secondary concerns are an undocumented ValueError that conflates developer error with client error, and a silent no-op when the value is already a list. Tests demonstrate happy paths but miss boundary invariants. Land with the cleanups.
